title: CNN Fundamentals
interviewAnswer: CNNs exploit local spatial structure with shared filters. Early layers learn local edges/textures, while deeper layers combine them into larger receptive-field features.
why: CNNs remain foundational for vision and help explain locality, parameter sharing, receptive fields and why 2D vs 3D architectures behave differently.
intuition: A convolution reuses the same small filter across locations, so the model learns patterns such as edges or textures regardless of where they appear.
deepDive: A convolution kernel slides across spatial dimensions, producing feature maps. Parameter sharing makes CNNs far more efficient than dense layers on images. Stride controls sampling; padding controls boundary/size behavior; dilation expands receptive field. Stacking layers builds hierarchical features and enlarges effective receptive field. Pooling/strided convolution reduce spatial resolution while increasing semantic abstraction.
workedExample: A 3×3 RGB filter has 3×3×3 weights per output channel, and the same weights are applied at every image location, unlike a fully connected layer with separate weights per pixel.
commonMistakes: Saying convolution is automatically translation invariant; it is more accurately translation equivariant before pooling/aggregation.
Assuming a large theoretical receptive field means all pixels contribute equally in practice.
followUps: What do stride and padding do?
production: Vision pipelines must keep resize/crop/normalization identical between training and serving. Throughput depends heavily on resolution, batch size and device kernels.

lab.goal: Build a small CNN and verify spatial/channel shapes.
lab.buildIt:
import torch
net=torch.nn.Sequential(
 torch.nn.Conv2d(1,8,3,padding=1),torch.nn.ReLU(),torch.nn.MaxPool2d(2),
 torch.nn.Conv2d(8,16,3,padding=1),torch.nn.ReLU(),torch.nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
 torch.nn.Flatten(),torch.nn.Linear(16,3))
x=torch.randn(4,1,64,64); print(net(x).shape)
lab.useIt:
# Inspect feature map shape explicitly.
features=net[:3](x); print(features.shape)  # [4, 8, 32, 32]

visual.caption: Convolution combines local connectivity and weight sharing, building progressively richer spatial features.
